title: Bulgaria's Budget Gamble: Record Borrowing Meets Stubborn Inflation in a Test… · 27 Aug
keywords: Bulgaria, budget 2026, fiscal deficit, public debt, GDP growth, inflation, European Commission, euro accession, SAFE instrument, cost of living, excessive deficit procedure, Bulgarian economy
notes: Bulgaria's parliament has approved a 2026 budget with a 5.7% deficit and up to 10.1 billion euros in new borrowing, triggering a fierce domestic political debate about fiscal discipline and the cost of living. The move comes as the European Commission has already flagged Sofia over excessive-deficit concerns, raising questions about the country's credibility on its path toward euro-area membership. Solid GDP growth of 2.7% in the second quarter of 2026 offers some reassurance, but persistent inflation and weak export performance mean the headline figures tell only part of the story for ordinary Bulgarians.
